G1.rationale: The Bachelor of Actuarial Science comprises 144 credit points structured into foundational commerce, discipline studies in actuarial modeling and econometrics, specialist actuarial studies/analytics, and electives, satisfying Actuaries Institute professional exemption standards.
evidenceLines: You must complete units as specified in Parts A, B, C and D (144 credit points): including 96 points of study in Parts A, B, C and 48 points of elective studies in Part D.
ETC1000 Business and economic statistics
ETC2410 Introductory econometrics
ETC2430 Actuarial cash flow modelling
ETC2520 Probability and statistical inference for economics and business
ETC2560 Statistical modelling for actuarial studies
ETC3550 Applied forecasting

G2.rationale: Core actuarial curriculum requires complex decision-making under stochastic uncertainty, life table mortality risk, and probabilistic modeling.
evidenceLines: develop extensions using life tables for the valuation of basic life insurance policies with stochastic cash-flows.
apply Bayesian models and credibility theory to insurance problems.
apply probability concepts to model uncertainty and assess risk in business and economic contexts

C1.rationale: Level 2 is met: team collaboration and group problem-solving are assessed in accounting tasks (ACC1100), statistical presentations (ETC1000), and actuarial project presentations (ETC2430: 3 - Presentation: 10%). Not level 3: human/AI collaboration division of labour is not explicitly assessed.
evidenceLines: collaborate effectively in team-based accounting tasks to contribute disciplinary knowledge and support collective problem solving
collaborating in teams to present evidence-based insights for business audiences
3 - Presentation: 10%

C2.rationale: Level 2 is met: quantitative project validation, statistical diagnostic testing, and model appraisal are assessed in ETC2430 (1 - Project: 20%) and ETC2560. Not level 3: criterion-referenced justification of AI or automated tool reliance is not documented in the core.
evidenceLines: 1 - Project: 20%
3 - Presentation: 10%

C3.rationale: Level 2 is met across the core: ETC3550 teaches computational forecasting with R, ETC2560 teaches Bayesian and generalised linear modeling, and ETC2410 teaches econometrics software. Not level 3: critique, ethics, and governance of AI systems are not mandated in the common degree core.
evidenceLines: You will enhance your computational skills with exercises using R.
ETC2560 Statistical modelling for actuarial studies

C4.rationale: Level 3 is sustained: core units in probability and inference (ETC2520), cash flow modeling (ETC2430), statistical modeling (ETC2560), and applied forecasting (ETC3550) demand advanced mathematical deduction, stochastic calculus, Bayesian inference, and complex computational modeling.
evidenceLines: develop extensions using life tables for the valuation of basic life insurance policies with stochastic cash-flows.
apply Bayesian models and credibility theory to insurance problems.
apply probability concepts to model uncertainty and assess risk in business and economic contexts

C5.rationale: Level 2 is met: rigorous multi-stage professional progression, actuarial institute syllabus testing, and adaptive problem-solving across deterministic and stochastic financial contexts.
evidenceLines: ETC2430 Actuarial cash flow modelling

W1.rationale: Level 2 is met: communicating statistical and actuarial findings to business audiences and professional stakeholders is explicitly taught and assessed in ETC1000 and ETC2430.
evidenceLines: collaborating in teams to present evidence-based insights for business audiences
3 - Presentation: 10%

W2.rationale: Level 2 is met: authentic financial and insurance cash flow project modeling in ETC2430 (1 - Project: 20%) applying industry life tables and annuity valuation.
evidenceLines: 1 - Project: 20%
develop extensions using life tables for the valuation of basic life insurance policies with stochastic cash-flows.

W3.rationale: Level 1 is met: while the handbook notes opportunities for industry-based experience as part of the specialisations, external workplace immersion is an elective/selective stream rather than compulsory for the degree as a whole.
evidenceLines: You must complete units as specified in Parts A, B, C and D (144 credit points): including 96 points of study in Parts A, B, C and 48 points of elective studies in Part D.

ambiguities: C1: Actuarial presentation and team tasks assess group presentation skills, but do not assess human/AI division of labour, resolving to level 2.
C3: Advanced machine learning techniques are available in the Actuarial Analytics stream, but the degree core is scored across common units (R computing in ETC3550), resolving to level 2.
W3: Industry-based experience is offered in specialist streams, but formal external placement is non-compulsory in the degree core, resolving to level 1.
